095154b8ddbfbf382eedb0cdf812444aee459813: Valloire offers 90 km of well-marked runs, a medium-sized ski area that's ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 17 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Valloire's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2,600 m and a village at 1,430 m, snow reliability in Valloire is generally dependable from January to late March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strain early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly with the first serious snowfalls. A Valloire stay is clearly on the expensive side: a 55€ day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the priciest in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short: Valloire is one of those rare resorts that combines a genuine village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It's hard to have a bad stay here.

09c8d486c3d18f7d38c2b96cb3e637100cffee76: Rothwald is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 25 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Rothwald's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. Rothwald's altitude (1750 m at the base, 2270 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover through the depths of winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The 46€ day lift pass places Rothwald among the mid-priced resorts — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Rothwald doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
